headline: Marie's south swell keeps it inside: halibut flats and Cruz backside
body:
No advisory covers the weekend — the current small craft advisory expires late Wednesday night — but Hurricane Marie is throwing a long-period south swell up the coast, and the outer waters stay ugly: 7 to 10 ft Saturday and 7 to 9 ft Sunday from Santa Cruz out to San Nicolas, with 14-second south sets stacked on NW wind chop. Wind is not the problem; the swell is. A chance of showers Sunday.

That kills the long runs. Osborn at 68 nm and San Nicolas at 73 nm both show 6-plus ft at the point, and Osborn's water is 71.5 °F — off the bluefin break anyway. Santa Rosa Flats is on temp at 65.9–66.4 °F but sits in 6.2–6.6 ft; not worth 40 nm in that slop.

Fish inside. The Goleta–Carpinteria flats are the sure thing both days — 2 to 6 kn, 3 ft, 68.9 °F on the 40–120 ft sand. Sunday is the better call for the backside of Santa Cruz: 4.2 ft, near-calm midday, and 71.9 °F for 80-ft troll lines, with rockfish on the hard patches as backup.
